meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Federal Common Law; Quebec Civil Law for private law matters under the Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c. CCQ-1991)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applicable 2017
Canada-China Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA), in force 2014

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA), as amended; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c. C-46, ss. 462.31 and 462.5; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c. C-44, ss. 21.1-21.4 (Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) transparent register regime effective from 22 January 2024). Provincial (Quebec): Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1 (QBCA), arts. 29-31 and 100 (register of directors and beneficial shareholders); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each director, officer, and individual with significant control (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioner of oaths duly licensed in the applicant's country of domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada acceded with effect from 11 January 2024; apostille issued by Global Affairs Canada for Canadian-origin documents or by the competent foreign authority for non-Canadian documents; Quebec-issued documents are apostilled by the Ministere de la Justice du Quebec)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing utility company or financial institution, countersigned by a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the document's country of issuance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incumbency for any corporate shareholder of the applicant entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-jurisdiction corporate registry (e.g., Companies House, applicable Secretary of State, or provincial registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the home-jurisdiction competent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax residence certificate / TIN certificate of each individual with significant control (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the home-jurisdiction competent authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and UBOs against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN), the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and Canadian sanctions enacted under the Special Economic Measures Act, RSC 1992, c. C-17, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2017, c. 21, and the Criminal Code; enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any person identified as a politically exposed person (PEP) under FINTRAC rules; negative screening results must be retained in the corporate minute book and refreshed prior to opening payment-rail accounts (Stripe, PayPal).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Federal: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (ised-isde.canada.ca / ISPRS). Provincial: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - Registre des entreprises (registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the mandatory language of the corporate name under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, arts. 21-29, 63-65, and the Regulation respecting the language of commerce and business, CQLR c. C-11, r. 9: a Quebec corporation or a federally incorporated corporation carrying on business in Quebec must have a name in French; permitted corporate suffixes include 'Inc.', 'Ltee', 'Corp.' and 'Corporation'; English trade names are only permissible if filed alongside a French version, and transliterated or anglicized variants require a NUANS phonetic equivalence analysis and, where used commercially, a registered French-language trade name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the incorporator obtains a fresh NUANS report (reports are valid for 90 days) and may file a written review application with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec under arts. 18-21 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, or with Corporations Canada for a federal incorporation; the request must include distinct proposed names, a legal argument on non-confusion under the Trademarks Act, RSC 1985, c. T-13, and any consent letters from prior name holders; if the registrar confirms the refusal, an appeal may be brought before the Court of Quebec within 30 days of notification of the final decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the statutory head office (siege social): QBCA art. 219 requires a physical location in Quebec where corporate books and records, including the share register and minutes, are accessible; the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec rejects virtual-mailbox-only addresses for registration; a virtual office is acceptable only as an auxiliary correspondence or operational address, not as the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 3-5% annual probability for an ISIC 4791 e-commerce operator with no physical retail premises and no statutory license; targeted unannounced verification by the REQ and audit activity by Revenu Quebec remain possible.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporations Canada / Registraire des entreprises du Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of CA$30 plus applicable indirect taxes

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Federal articles of incorporation filing fee (CBCA, online filing)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of CA$200 for online filings under CBCA

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Quebec declaration of registration (extra-provincial registration of a federal corporation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee of CA$45 plus statutory publication charge under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille bundle for identification, address proof, and corporate good-standing documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed notary public + Global Affairs Canada / Ministere de la Justice du Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate of approximately CA$150 notarial fees plus CA$15 per apostille certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register and corporate records minute book (ISC register, share register, bylaws, and consents)
Registered office (siege social) address and corporate mail-handling service in Quebec - 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate of CA$350-CA$500 per annum

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: French-language compliance review of corporate name and trade-name usage (Charter of the French Language)
Legal incorporation, UBO piercing review, PEP/sanctions screening, and shareholder resolutions - fixed professional fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a low-risk e-commerce holding structure

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), C.Q.L.R. c. S-31.1, particularly sections 9–20 (incorporation), section 27 (articles), and section 55 (registered office); supplemented by regulations under the Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises (Québec Enterprise Registrar), Government of Quebec
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Articles constitutifs), filed electronically via the Registraire des entreprises' CliquezAffaires online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required under the QBCA. The corporation may issue shares for cash, property, or past services provided the issuance is solvent. No escrow account is mandated; however, banks may require a nominal deposit certificate to open a corporate bank account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the first common shares of the corporation (500 common shares) be subscribed and issued to the founding shareholder for cash consideration, such payment to be made to the corporate bank account upon opening. RESOLVED that the registered office of the corporation be fixed at 1200 Rue de la Montagne, Montréal, Quebec, H3G 1Z2, and that the Registrar be authorized to record such address. RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed as President and Chief Executive Officer, and [Name] as Corporate Secretary, each to hold office until removed or successors elected. All officers are authorized to execute and file any documentation required by law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises – online name reservation window (CliquezAffaires)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search and submit a reservation request through the Registraire des entreprises' online portal. The name must contain a legal element such as 'Inc.' or 'Corp.' and must be distinguishable from existing names in Quebec. Upon approval, the reservation certificate is valid for 60 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit an alternative name or file a written appeal to the Registraire's legal services for reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Quebec notary or independent legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of incorporation in French or bilingual format, including the corporate name, share structure and any restrictions, registered office address, initial directors, and any limitation on business. For a non-online filing, the articles must be signed by the incorporator and notarized. The notary will also prepare the initial director consent form (CO-01).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the articles are rejected or incomplete, the notary or counsel shall correct the document and recommence the notarial execution process without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing with the Registraire des Entreprises and Issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarized articles and the director consent form to the CliquezAffaires portal. Pay the $200 CAD filing fee plus registration fee. Upon successful review, the Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the initial enterprise number (NEQ). This filing also serves as the obligatory initial registration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (electronic or scanned)
Any by-law initial draft referenced in articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is refused for non-compliance, the applicant must resubmit a corrected package within 10 days; an administrative review can be requested if the refusal is perceived to be erroneous.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations with Revenu Québec and CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and the Canada Revenue Agency (through Business Registration Online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for Quebec Sales Tax (QST, TVQ), federal Goods and Services Tax (GST/HST), and, where applicable, payroll deductions using the new Business Number and enterprise number. Provide these registrations to the corporate bank when opening a corporate account. Registration is effective immediately; the corporation must begin collecting QST/GST once sales commence.
required_dossiers: Directors' personal name, address, date of birth and social insurance numbers
Bank account details or pending account confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, assess late-filing penalties under the Taxation Act and apply for relief under section 22 of the Tax Administration Act showing good faith and minor harm.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting, Share Subscription and Statutory Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the corporation (with advise of corporate secretary and external counsel)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting. Adopt the pro-forma resolution (above) to issue shares, fix the registered office, and appoint officers. Approve the model by-laws, adopt share certificate forms, authorize bank signing authorities, and complete the minute book. Issue share certificates to the founding shareholder after subscription payment.
required_dossiers: First board resolution minutes (incl. share subscription, registered office, officers)
Share subscription agreement or bank payment evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If by-laws are not adopted at the initial meeting, directors may pass a subsequent written resolution ratifying the by-laws and apply retroactively to the date of the first meeting.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure online retail; however, ancillary warehousing or repair operations may engage the Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) for construction/occupancy permits and the Ministry of Economy and Innovation (MEEI) for any innovation programn.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no statutory operating license is required for e-commerce retail of consumer electronics in Quebec; optional e-waste collection registration may apply under RECYC-QUÉBEC's electronics stewardship program.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the proposed activity (online retail, no industrial manufacturing or processing) falls under Category II of the Regulation respecting the environmental impact assessment and review; no full EIA or registration report is required unless warehousing of hazardous wastes occurs.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For minimal office and storage operations, compliance with municipal sewer discharge thresholds for conventional pollutants; product waste (batteries, electronic components) must be handled under Quebec EPR (extended producer responsibility) rules, and batteries must be delivered to certified recycling facilities per the Regulation respecting batteries. Packaging must fulfill recycling and reduction obligations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the municipal fire prevention department for the registered office; structural load inspection certificate for any storage area beyond office use; and CNESST (Quebec occupational health and safety board) incident-free workplace certification for employees, including a basic health and safety program for those engaged in warehousing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST and income tax; Revenu Québec for Quebec corporate income tax, QST, and provincial registrations. Portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html) and Revenu Québec's Cl@R Affaires (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate federally or provincially under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) or Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA). 2. Obtain the federal Business Number (BN) from CRA by submitting Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) online through the CRA ‘Business Registration Online’ (BRO) service, or by mail/fax. 3. Register for GST/HST and, if applicable, payroll and corporate income tax accounts using the same RC1 form. 4. In parallel, register with Revenu Québec for the Quebec Provincial Identification Number (NEQ) and QST registration via the ‘Registraire d’entreprises’ (REQ) and the Cl@R Affaires portal. 5. Non-resident corporations must also provide the authorized representative information (Form RC2 for the BN, Form LM-11 for QST). 6. Upon registration, the entity receives a 9‑digit BN program identifier (e.g., BN '123456789 RT0001') and a separate QST file number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Canadian tax law. Canadian corporations are taxed at the entity level under Part I of the Income Tax Act (Canada). For Quebec, the Corporation Tax Act imposes separate entity-level tax. Certain ministerial elections are available, such as the election to treat a wholly-owned subsidiary as a branch for foreign accrual property income (FAPI) purposes (s. 218.1), the capital dividend account election (s. 83(2)), and the joint election for wind-up of a subsidiary (s. 88(1.3)). However, these do not alter the fundamental entity-level classification. Additionally, Quebec rules follow the federal classification; no hybrid mismatch election is available for non-resident entities. Hybrid mismatch rules (ITA s. 18.4 to 18.7) apply to disallow deductions in cross-border arrangements but do not require an affirmative election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) – value-added style consumption taxes
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (small supplier threshold) – applies when taxable supplies exceed this amount in any single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters; Canadian resident corporations, other than small suppliers, must register. For non-resident digital services providers, a separate economic nexus threshold of CAD 30,000 from supplies to Canadian consumers also applies. Quebec’s QST threshold is the same, administered by Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time electronic clearance or fiscal stamping exists in Canada. The CRA and Revenu Québec accept electronic invoices (e.g., PDF, XML) as long as they contain prescribed information (Excise Tax Act s. 223, QST rules under Quebec Taxation Act). For GST/HST, the supplier must issue an invoice or simplified invoice if the taxable supply exceeds CAD 150. Suppliers using electronic systems must retain records in machine-readable format; CRA audits typically require system access via API integrations for data extraction. Voluntary B2B e-invoicing standards (e.g., EDI, Peppol) are recognized, but no government-operated clearance portal is mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: To claim a 0% GST/HST (and QST) rate for exported goods, the supplier must be a registrant, the goods must be sold to a non-resident purchaser, and the goods must be delivered or shipped to a destination outside Canada by the supplier (or through an agent) for direct export. Services (including online electronic services) are zero-rated when provided to a non-resident, but only if the service is not performed in Canada or is not otherwise supplied to a person who is resident in Canada at any time, and the service does not relate to real property in Canada or to tangible personal property situated in Canada. In Quebec, parallel QST zero-rating applies under the Quebec Taxation Act s. 403 and following.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (for goods exported from Canada, as per the Customs Act, reporting requirement)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing transportation to the foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement showing receipt of payment in foreign currency from the non-resident customer
Commercial invoice issued to the non-resident buyer with the seller’s BN and QST registration number, explicit '0% exported' indicator
Proof of export (e.g., export packer list, customs broker report, or Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) electronic export data via the Canadian Export Reporting System (CES))
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec routinely audit export zero-rating claims, requiring the exporter to maintain full documentation trails. If the 180-day repatriation deadline is missed, or if documentation is incomplete, the CRA will disallow the zero-rating and reassess the supply at 5% GST (plus 9.975% QST in Quebec) and levy 'goods and services tax/HST rebate' recovery plus interest. Penalties under Excise Tax Act s. 280.1 range from 10% to 25% of the net tax amount for false statements or willful participation in a misstatement. For fraudulent export schemes, criminal penalties can include fines up to 200% of the tax attempted to be evaded and imprisonment up to five years, as well as retroactive clawback of all input tax credits claimed on export-related expenses. Revenu Québec imposes similar penalties under the Quebec Taxation Act s. 1129.1.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a floating exchange rate regime with unrestricted convertibility for current account transactions, including trade settlements, service payments, and profit remittances. Capital account transactions require Bank of Canada approval only in narrowly defined cases; for legitimate corporate activities, convertibility is unrestricted. Profit remittance is permitted upon submission of corporate resolutions, audited financial statements, and tax filings, with no material regulatory hurdles for Quebec-incorporated entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement exists for mandatory surrender of export proceeds under Canadian law. Exporters must file export declarations with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) within 30 days of shipment and retain supporting documentation. Banks may request proof of export (commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading) for transactions exceeding CAD 10,000 to satisfy FINTRAC AML obligations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility rating for regulated electronic money issuers such as Stripe and PayPal. Legal constraints are confined to compliance with the Payment Services Act, FINTRAC AML registration, and PIPEDA data protection requirements. Offshore digital EMIs are permissible provided the platform holds appropriate Canadian licenses or operates under approved partnerships.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate account opening is fully permitted under Canadian federal and provincial regulations using electronic KYC verification and DocuSign-style e-signatures. Physical presence of directors is not required for standard onboarding; remote processes are acceptable unless the account involves high-value or cross-border transactions exceeding FINTRAC thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions linked to high-risk jurisdictions or unexplained source of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate minute authorizing the account, beneficial ownership declaration, source-of-funds letter, and registration certificates from Corporations Canada or Quebec Enterprise Registrar

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound remittances exceeding CAD 10,000 without supporting trade documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Export contracts, commercial invoices, proof of shipment, CBSA export declaration, and corporate resolution confirming legitimate business purpose

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections are executed via SWIFT wire transfers using purpose codes 'EQUITY CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN'. Verification requires corporate charter, shareholder agreement, beneficial ownership certificate, and proof of tax residency. All remittances must comply with FINTRAC reporting thresholds and be routed through Canadian-dollar or multi-currency accounts at Tier-1 banks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements are cleared via SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit. Required documentation includes commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, and CBSA export compliance evidence. All transactions must reference the corporate account number and purpose code aligned with the underlying trade contract.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Quebec Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the corporation's fiscal year-end (or anniversary of registration if fiscal year not declared)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee surcharge (approximately CAD 29–59); failure to file for 2 consecutive years triggers cancellation of registration or administrative dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month (max 12%); interest on outstanding balances; Quebec adds provincial penalty and interest; repeated non-filing may lead to administrative dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Not mandatory for small private corporations if all shareholders consent in writing to waive the appointment of an auditor; mandatory for reporting issuers (public) or when shareholders holding at least 10% of voting shares request an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises, Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook); IFRS required for public reporting issuers.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: All changes to shareholding or persons with significant control (25% or more voting rights or financial interest) must be entered in the company's statutory register and reflected in the annual declaration filed with the REQ. The declaration confirms the share structure and control information as of the filing date.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–10,000 for a review engagement; USD 10,000–25,000 for a full audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal and Quebec general corporate income tax rate: 26.5% (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) with qualifying active business income is eligible for the federal small business deduction on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income, reducing the federal rate to 9%; Quebec provides a corresponding reduced rate of 3% on the first CAD 500,000. This yields a combined 12% effective rate on the initial taxable bracket for eligible CCPCs. No broad statutory tax holidays apply to online retail operations, but investment tax credits, refundable credits, and prior-year loss application (non-capital losses carried back 3 years and forward 20 years) can materially reduce effective taxation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return – filed electronically through the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) e-File system or certified tax software; paper filing is available by mail for non-mandatory filers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Every corporation carrying on business or having taxable income in Canada must file a T2 return even if no tax is payable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the end of the fiscal period. A corporation with a December 31 year-end must file by June 30 of the following year. Non-resident corporations with Canadian-source business income must adhere to the same six-month filing deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The nine-digit CRA business number and two-digit corporate income tax account code. All corporate tax accounts, filings, and remittances are referenced under this number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation must obtain a BN and register as a non-resident corporation under account code RC0001, indicating its agent for service in Canada if required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net income from financial statements reconciled to tax rules under the Income Tax Act, including gross revenue from online sales, COGS, operating expenses, and amortization adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation files only Canadian-source income attributable to carrying on business in Canada; foreign income is excluded unless treaty reallocation or permanent establishment rules trigger inclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after applying non-capital loss carryforwards, capital loss carryforwards, dividends received subject to dividend deduction, and other specific deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers may deduct loss carryforwards only to the extent they relate to the Canadian business or permanent establishment; restrictions under subsection 111(7) apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Base federal tax computed at 15% of taxable income, reduced by the small business deduction for eligible CCPCs and by federal tax credits (e.g., foreign tax credits, investment tax credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations are not eligible for the federal small business deduction; they compute 15% branch tax on Canadian taxable income and may claim only treaty-based or specifically applicable credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under subsection 162(1) of the Income Tax Act: the greater of CAD 100 and 5% of the unpaid tax, plus an additional 1% per complete month of unpaid tax for up to 12 months. For a second occurrence, the penalty is 10% of unpaid tax. Prescribed interest accrues on all balances, and criminal prosecution may apply for wilful omissions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return – filed separately with Revenu Québec via its electronic filing portal (CLICK) or approved tax software. The CO-17 reconciles the federal T2 computation with Quebec-specific tax rules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, covering the same taxation year as the federal T2 return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the end of the fiscal period. For a December 31 year-end, the Quebec return is due June 30. A non-resident corporation with a Quebec establishment must file within the same deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) assigned by the Registraire des entreprises and identification of the corporation, registered office, and place of business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation must register the Quebec establishment before filing and indicate the person authorized to receive notifications in Quebec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted federal net income, incorporating Quebec-specific provisions for depreciation, amortization, and other adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only income reasonably attributable to the Quebec establishment is included; income outside Quebec is excluded after proper allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income after allocating income among provinces and applying Quebec loss carryover rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For e-commerce, the allocation factor considers Quebec gross sales, full-time equivalent employees, and payroll; warehousing or delivery operations in Quebec may create a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec corporate tax computed at 11.5% for general corporations or 3% for qualifying CCPCs on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income, plus the health contribution if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations pay Quebec tax at the general 11.5% rate on taxable income allocated to Quebec; no small business deduction is available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec imposes a late filing penalty equal to 5% of the unpaid Quebec corporate tax plus 1% per full month of default, up to 12 months, together with interest. A repeated failure triggers 10%. Civil and criminal remedies under the Taxation Act (RLRQ, c. I-3) parallel the federal rules.
